newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan budget sees one pct drop in GDP in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan budget sees one pct drop in GDP in 1997.

text.p: Morocco's 1997/98 draft budget forecasts a drop of one percent in real gross domestic product in 1997 because of drought, compared with growth of 11.8 percent in 1996, the official MAP news agency said on Wednesday.
Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj is expected to present details of the draft budget for the year to June 30, 1998, to parliament on Wednesday evening, an official said.

The Casablanca-based independent Centre Marocain de Conjoncture think-tank earlier said Morocco's economy "may stagnate or drop to minus one percent in 1997, from 11.8 percent growth in 1996, due mainly to the declining trend of agriculture output this year."
Agriculture represents nearly 20 percent of Morocco's GDP and employs 50 percent of the country's estimated 10 million workforce.

Morocco harvested 10 million tonnes of cereals in 1995/96 against 1.6 million tonnes in 1994/95 season after it was hit by a severe drought described by the authorities as "the drought of the century".
